title: Service reliability stakeholder runway and escalation proposal
content:
Purpose:
This proposal outlines a 10-week cross-functional runway to operationalize SLOs for model-serving products and to establish a lightweight, repeatable escalation matrix and runbook for on-call responders and product stakeholders. The focus is on practical outcomes: clear SLO definitions and ownership, automated error-budget signal plumbing, capacity safety thresholds, and a tested escalation flow that reduces mean time to decision for degraded serving conditions.

Scope and out-of-band assumptions:
- In scope: model-serving API endpoints (text generation, chat, embeddings) and the Redis-backed prefix cache layer. Includes telemetry (latency p95/p99, error rate, queue depth), incident-to-SLO feedback loop, and runbook automation for automated tiered escalation.
- Out of scope: billing changes, Dedicated contract negotiation, third-party observability vendor replacement.
- Assumptions: telemetry streams available via observability pipeline (OTLP -> Loki/Tempo/Prometheus); capacity telemetry from autoscaler already emitted to our metrics topic; on-call rotations staffed across SRE and Platform-Eng.

High-level goals (success criteria):
1) SLOs published for 6 canonical services (API-gen, chat-router, embeddings, prefix-cache, routing-proxy, request-queue) with owners and target error budgets.
2) Automated error-budget alerts (Slack + PagerDuty) that map to runbook actions and update the SLO dashboard.
3) Escalation matrix with decision thresholds (green/amber/red) and well-tested runbook play for amber-to-red transition.
4) Capacity safety policy defined: automated throttling or fallback model routing when capacity hits 80% sustained utilization for 5+ minutes.
5) 2 tabletop exercises that include SRE, Platform Eng, Product Hosted API, and Solutions Eng.

Stakeholders and roles:
- Project lead (SRE): Asha Patel — orchestration, scheduling, cross-team coordination.
- Platform Eng lead: Marco Diaz — capacity policy implementation, autoscaler hooks.
- Product Hosted API PM: Priya Shah — product impact, customer comms.
- Observability owner: Sofia Nguyen — metrics, dashboards, alert rules.
- Solutions Eng rep: Liam O'Connor — customer-facing play validation.
- Escalation approvers: Head of SRE, Head of Platform (for formal sign-off).

Timeline and milestones (10-week runway):
Week 0 (kickoff): align on scope, confirm owners, add Jira epic (RWI-621).
Week 1-2: SLO drafts for each service + owner sign-off. Create confluence page with SLO definitions and test checklist.
Week 3: Implement Prometheus recording rules and synthetic tests for SLO signals.
Week 4-5: Wire alerts to Slack + PagerDuty; create automated remediation hooks (abort/route fallback).
Week 6: Define capacity safety policy and implement autoscaler threshold experiment (canary).
Week 7: Author runbook playbooks and map to PagerDuty escalation policies.
Week 8: Run first tabletop (inject latency + error spike scenario). Capture gaps and assign actions.
Week 9: Implement fixes from retro, tighten alert thresholds.
Week 10: Final sign-off, publish SLOs, and handoff to steady-state operations.

Detailed deliverables and owners:
- SLO spec document (one page per service): owner Sofia Nguyen + Asha Patel. Checklist: intent, user journey, measurement window, numerator/denominator, error budget policy.
- Metrics plumbing: Prom record rules, tagging schema (service, model, tenant): owner Sofia Nguyen.
- Dashboard: SLO burn rate widget, per-tenant latency histogram, error budget trend: owner Sofia.
- Alerting: 3 tiers — advisory (Slack), action (pager to on-call), escalation (exec/pgm notify). Owner: Asha + PagerDuty admin.
- Capacity Safety Policy: 80% sustained, 30% single-host-buffer, fallback to cheaper model variants. Owner: Marco Diaz.
- Runbooks: play-by-play for amber and red incidents (check KV cache, route fallback, scale up, contact SRE on-call, notify product): owner Liam O'Connor.
- Tabletop exercise plan and report: owner Asha.

Playbook: amber-to-red escalation (short version)
- Amber (service-level p99 latency > SLO for 3 min OR error rate > 2x baseline for 5 min): slack advisory to service channel, create incident stub. SRE on-call runs quick checks (recent deploys, hot shards). If mitigation is a config toggle, apply and monitor for 2 minutes.
- Red (p99 > SLO for 10 min OR error budget burn rate > 50%/hour): page SRE primary, page Platform Eng, run fallback routing policy (route 20% of traffic to cheaper model variant), enable autoscaler emergency policy (+30% capacity). Notify Product PM and Solutions Eng.
- Post-incident: incident -> SLO retro within 3 business days, create corrective actions, link to SLO panel.

Communication and decision channels:
- Operational comms: #sre-ops (real-time), #serving-incident (cross-team incident comms).
- Weekly sync: SRE x Platform weekly 30m on Thursday for runway progress.
- Executive escalation: email distribution list "service-reliability@redwood.ai" + on-call pager escalation to service owner leads.
- Customer comms template: brief, impact, mitigation steps, expected ETA for restoration (owned by Product PM Priya Shah).

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: noisy signals cause pager fatigue. Mitigation: two-stage alerting with advisory Slack first and short cooldown; synthetic checks to correlate real user impact before paging.
- Risk: capacity policy triggers degrade output quality (fallback to smaller model). Mitigation: define quality budget and automated A/B smoke test during fallback to ensure basic correctness thresholds.
- Risk: ownership confusion between Platform Eng and SRE. Mitigation: explicit ownership table on confluence and runbook with step-by-step handoffs.

Acceptance criteria for sign-off:
- All 6 SLO pages published with explicit owners and measurement queries.
- Alerts wired and verified in staging with synthetic failure test.
- Escalation matrix documented and validated in 2 tabletop exercises with checklist completion.
- Capacity policy instrumented in an isolated canary and validated under 2 synthetic load profiles.
- Postmortem / SLO retro workflow created and linked from incident template.

Next steps (immediate):
- Kickoff meeting scheduled (Asha) for 2026-11-05 10:00 PT.
- Add initial subtasks to epic RWI-621: SLO spec, metrics plumbing, alerts, capacity experiment.
- Slack poll for tabletop participant windows (Asha).

Open questions for the kickoff (to discuss):
1) Which measurement window for embeddings latency is most representative for downstream customers (30s sliding vs 5m rolling)?
2) How aggressive should the fallback routing be by default (10%/20%/50%) for production?
3) Should Solutions Eng own the customer-facing validation for fallback quality or should we create a lightweight automated smoke harness?

Appendix: quick-reference owners table (for runbook):
- API-gen: Owner: Sofia Nguyen; Escalation: SRE on-call -> Marco Diaz
- Prefix-cache: Owner: Marco Diaz; Escalation: Platform Eng -> SRE lead
- Routing-proxy: Owner: Liam O'Connor; Escalation: Platform Eng

Notes: This document is intentionally pragmatic and written as a working proposal. Expect iteration after the first tabletop where we will fold in learnings and update thresholds and ownership flows.

References and artifacts to review before kickoff:
- Confluence SLO template: https://confluence.redwood.ai/pages/viewpage.action?pageId=9876543
- Jira epic: RWI-621 (linked above)
- Example dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/serving/slo-burnrate
